subject.title: Feature Request: Support YAML as config file format

question: Should OpenClaw expand the stable core config contract to accept `openclaw.yaml`/`openclaw.yml`, or keep JSON5 as the only first-party config file format and improve the safe editing guidance instead?
rationale: The request is clear and technically feasible, but it changes a stable core configuration surface and needs an intentional product/compatibility decision before implementation.

options.title: Keep JSON5-only for now
options.body: Close or leave this as a declined product direction after documenting the preferred comment-safe mutation paths through `openclaw config`, `config.patch`, and targeted editors.

options.title: Sponsor YAML support
options.body: Accept the new config format only with a design covering precedence, parse coercion, write-back behavior, doctor recovery, docs, and upgrade tests.

recommendation.title: Keep JSON5-only for now
recommendation.body: Close or leave this as a declined product direction after documenting the preferred comment-safe mutation paths through `openclaw config`, `config.patch`, and targeted editors.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows the strongest overlap with config docs, parser behavior, and CLI config semantics that this product choice would affect.
